item.title: A Search in LHCb Open Data for $f$-Baryon Resonances Predicted at HADRON 2025
item.description: arXiv:2610.37674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A prediction presented at HADRON 2025 proposed two baryon-like states containing an additional hypothesized $f$ quark that could appear in the decay $\Bbar\to\Lb\Lc K^-$ in the form of narrow $\Lc K^-$ resonances at 3800 and 3950~MeV. Public LHCb data are used here to compare three hypotheses with an unbinned, background-aware two-dimensional Dalitz likelihood. The baseline contains nonresonant three-body phase space and an $N(1900)$ contribution in $\Lb K^-$. A second model tests the two a-priori prediction masses directly, fixing $\Lc K^-$ resonances at 3800 and 3950~MeV while fitting their widths. A third model keeps the 3800-MeV mass fixed, allows the second $\Lc K^-$ mass and width to float, and adds two exotic $\Lc\Lb$ contributions. The second model gives a nominal Wilks-equivalent improvement of $4.02\sigma$ over the baseline, while the third gives a nominal value of $6.17\sigma$. The quoted significances are model-comparison diagnostics only: the resonance fractions are constrained to be non-negative, some fitted widths reach parameter boundaries, the floating mass introduces a trials effect, and efficiency and systematic uncertainties are not yet incorporated.

item.title: The Position Resolution of a Charged Particle Hodoscope Consisting of Triangular Scintillator Counters
item.description: arXiv:2610.37955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hodoscopes consisting of triangular counters with embedded wavelength shifting fibers are becoming more popular as they are relatively inexpensive, are easily fabricated, need no cooling systems, employ low-cost photodetectors, require only modest voltages, and perhaps most importantly, have good position resolution. Through interpolation of the light yields between adjacent counters, position resolutions that are typically an order of magnitude better than the counter separation can be obtained. Here, after a brief explanation of how the interpolation is done to improve the position resolution, we derive an approximate expressions for the uncertainty in the interpolated $x$ and $y$ positions as a function of the impact position of the charged particle.

item.title: Amplitude analysis of the charmed baryon decay Lambda_c+ to p K_S^0 pi0
item.description: arXiv:2610.38406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using $e^+e^-$ annihilation data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 4.5 fb$^{-1}$ collected with the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies between 4.600 and 4.699 GeV, the first amplitude analysis of the charmed baryon decay $\Lambda_c^+ \to p K_S^0 \pi^0$ is performed. The processes $\Lambda_c^+ \to p \bar{K}^{*}(892)^0$, $\Lambda_c^+ \to \Delta(1600)^+ K_S^0$, and $\Lambda_c^+ \to N(1710)^+ K_S^0$ are identified with statistical significances of $12.8\sigma$, $14.5\sigma$, and $6.2\sigma$, respectively. The mass and width of $\Delta(1600)^+$ are measured to be $(1520.4 \pm 8.8 \pm 37.7)~\text{MeV}$ and $(199.4 \pm 26.4 \pm 39.9)~\text{MeV}$, respectively. The mass and width of $N(1710)^+$ are measured to be $(1719.7 \pm 9.4 \pm 9.1)~\text{MeV}$ and $(72.0 \pm 18.0 \pm 15.0)~\text{MeV}$, respectively. The branching fractions of these processes are determined to be $\mathcal{B}[\Lambda_c^+ \rightarrow \Delta(1600)^+ (\rightarrow p \pi^0) K_S^0] = (8.10 \pm 0.80 \pm 5.57) \times 10^{-3}$, $\mathcal{B}[\Lambda_c^+ \rightarrow N(1710)^+ (\rightarrow p \pi^0) K_S^0] = (1.58 \pm 0.48 \pm 0.77) \times 10^{-3}$, and $\mathcal{B}[\Lambda_c^+ \rightarrow p \bar{K}^{*}(892)^0 (\rightarrow K_S^0 \pi^0)] = (2.63 \pm 0.47 \pm 0.29) \times 10^{-3}$, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second systematic.

item.title: The TAMBO Project and the TAMBITO Prototype
item.description: arXiv:2610.38777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection of astrophysical PeV-scale neutrinos by IceCube and KM3NeT observatories has opened the window to probe new phenomena in the universe. However, a deeper study of the sources remains limited by the small astrophysical flux and the sizable atmospheric neutrino background. The Tau Air-Shower Mountain-Based Observatory (TAMBO) aims to overcome these limitations by detecting tau neutrinos from 1\,PeV to 1\,000\,PeV, an energy range in which backgrounds are largely suppressed and which lies between the reach of optical-Cherenkov observatories and that of radio-based experiments. TAMBO will employ up to 5,000 particle detectors installed on the face of a steep hill in the Colca Valley (Per\'u) to detect tau neutrinos interacting with the face of the canyon in front via the decay products of the associated tau leptons. In this contribution, we will describe the current status of the project and its R\&D, focusing on the 100-unit array TAMBITO prototype, the projected timeline, and the physics potential that this unique detector brings to the field.

item.title: Measurements of transverse kinematic imbalance in muon neutrino charged-current interactions on argon with a single proton and no pions in the final state with SBND
item.description: arXiv:2610.39042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter presents the first neutrino-argon cross-section measurement from the Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory. We report the nominal flux-averaged single-differential cross sections of muon neutrino charged-current interactions on argon with a single proton and no pions in the final state as functions of the transverse kinematic imbalance variables. Using a subset of Run~1 data corresponding to $8.8\times10^{19}$ protons-on-target, we select 12,804 signal candidates with a purity of 91%. The extracted cross sections discriminate strongly among event-generator predictions, owing to the high statistics and the design of the analysis. Among the compared models, none successfully describes all three variables, with the largest discrepancies in the transverse missing momentum variable. These results set new benchmarks for neutrino-argon interaction modeling, which is crucial for high-precision measurements at current and future accelerator neutrino experiments.

item.title: Dark sector searches at BESIII
item.description: arXiv:2610.39618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large samples of charmonia, charm mesons, hyperons and light mesons collected by BESIII offer sensitive tests of dark sector interactions with charm and light quarks. This contribution reviews recent searches for sub-GeV dark matter in $\eta\to\pi^0+\mathrm{invisible}$ and $J/\psi\to\phi+\mathrm{invisible}$, massless dark photons in $D^0\to\omega\gamma'$ and $D^0\to\gamma\gamma'$, invisible $K^0_S$ decays, dark baryons in $\Xi^-\to\pi^-\chi$, and light vector bosons in $\chi_{cJ}\to J/\psi V$, $V\to e^+e^-$. Particular attention is given to the $\eta$ search, which constrains scalar-mediated dark matter and tests thermal relic benchmarks.

item.title: Dark-field Search for Quantum Vacuum Signals in the Low-Energy Regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.39867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on the experimental details of a dark-field search for light-by-light scattering signals performed at the High Energy Density (HED) instrument of the European XFEL (EuXFEL) in a pump-probe type experiment colliding the EuXFEL beam with the 300-TW-class near-infrared Relativistic Laser at XFEL (ReLaX) at a center-of-mass photon energy of $\omega_\star = 116\,\mathrm{eV}$. Especially in combination with polarization filtering, the dark-field concept allows the signal-to-background ratio to be significantly enhanced and both polarization channels to be recorded. This work elaborates on the experimental setup and the diagnostics used, from the per-shot spatiotemporal-overlap diagnostics, via the polarizing beam splitter, to the characterization of the residual background. Moreover, it provides details on the start-to-end simulations of the setup used for analysis. Accumulating 2751 pump-probe collisions, no excess above background is observed, and an upper limit on the light-by-light scattering cross section of $7\times10^{4}$ times the QED prediction at a 95% confidence level is derived. This is the most stringent bound on low-energy light-by-light scattering achieved to date, representing an improvement by ten orders of magnitude upon previous experimental limits.

item.title: First search for sidereal and annual modulation of $Z$-pole asymmetries with the recovered SLD data set
item.description: arXiv:2610.40282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report what is, to our knowledge, the first time-resolved analysis of electroweak asymmetries at the $Z$ pole, using the public release of the recovered SLD collision data: $6.6\times10^5$ polarized $e^+e^-\to Z$ events from the 1996-1998 SLC runs, with 385583 selected hadronic $Z$ decays spanning 782 sidereal cycles. The left-right asymmetry $A_{LR}$, reconstructed with the published SLD selection and per-event signed Compton polarization, shows no sidereal, solar-diurnal, or annual modulation; a simultaneous unbinned likelihood fit bounds the sidereal first-harmonic amplitude at 0.0086 (95% C.L., statistical). The analysis, frozen on the initial partial release, applied unchanged to the 229833 events of the later-released 1998 run confirms the null (amplitude 0.0018, p=0.90). Using the as-built SLC beam azimuth from the release's documentation corpus, we bound the asymmetry's anisotropy tensor in the Sun-centered frame: $\rho_1\le0.060$, $\rho_2\le0.18$, and, for vector backgrounds, $\rho_0\le0.092$ (95% C.L.). A leading-order matching maps these onto minimal Standard-Model-Extension coefficients as $10^{-2}$-level sensitivities to the two-time-index block of the electroweak gauge-sector coefficient $k_W$ (components with no existing laboratory constraint) and to the Higgs-sector coefficient $k_{\phi\phi}$; the insertions split the $Z$ pole by polarization, so for the tensor families assessed the resonance saturates the sidereal amplitude near $10^{-2}$ and the Born-model bounds exclude finite coefficient bands rather than set an upper limit. We also derive a previously unpublished $Z$-pole birefringence channel in the helicity-odd azimuthal modulation of the thrust axis, with response enhanced by about $2M_Z/\Gamma_Z$; a Born-level pilot is null. First sidereal analyses of hadronization and leptonic asymmetries bound instrumental drifts at the $10^{-4}$-$10^{-3}$ fractional level.

item.title: FCC-\mu e: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN
item.description: arXiv:2610.40451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $\mu^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including the exciting prospect of measurements of the Higgs boson self-interaction, and is followed by a presentation of the FCC-$\mu e$ layout -- from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$\mu e$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.
item.dc:creator: K. Piotrzkowski

item.title: chATLAS: A Retrieval-Augmented Conversational Assistant for the ATLAS Experiment
item.description: arXiv:2610.37697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large scientific collaborations produce extensive internal documentation spread across heterogeneous systems, making it difficult for collaborators to locate and reuse existing knowledge. We present chATLAS, a deployed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant developed for the ATLAS experiment at CERN. The system provides conversational access to more than 30,000 documents from several collaboration resources, material largely unavailable to general-purpose language models, using hybrid dense--sparse retrieval deployed on CERN infrastructure. A domain-specific benchmark built from automatically generated question--answer pairs is used to evaluate retrieval and generation performance and to guide design choices. We study the selection and domain-specific fine-tuning of an embedding model, contextual retrieval, ranking strategies, and generator choice. Fine-tuning combined with contextual retrieval more than doubles how often the correct document is returned as the top result on the most technically challenging documentation source. The deployed system also includes intent routing, safety handling, Mattermost integration, and an MCP server for future agentic workflows. chATLAS demonstrates that domain-adapted RAG can provide source-attributed, domain-specific access to collaboration knowledge, and offers a practical foundation for scientific collaborations and other organisations that rely on accurate, up-to-date retrieval from proprietary documentation.

item.title: Model-Independent Determination of Intrinsic Leptonic CP Violation
item.description:
arXiv:2610.37744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Establishing leptonic Charge-Parity (CP) violation is a central goal of the next generation of long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. To achieve this, experimental analyses focus on excluding the CP-conserving values $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=0,\pi$ within the standard three-neutrino framework. We propose instead to establish CP violation as a phenomenon in a model-independent way. We use Gaussian Process regression to infer the $

u_e$ and $ ar

u_e$ appearance probabilities in a parametrization-free manner at DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande. By combining the two experiments, with mild assumptions on how matter impacts oscillations, we estimate how they can probe intrinsic CP violation in neutrino oscillations together. Taking the standard three-neutrino framework as a benchmark, we show that these experiments, when combined, can establish model-independent CP violation at $3\sigma$ for over 60% of the values of $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$.

item.title: End-to-end Particle Reconstruction with Transformers in High-Granularity Calorimeters
item.description: arXiv:2610.37798v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) will drastically increase the number of simultaneously interacting particles, posing a severe challenge to current particle reconstruction methods. While next-generation highly granular calorimeters offer unprecedented 3D measurement capabilities, reconstructing particles from heavily overlapping energy showers remains computationally difficult. This study investigates how raw detector hits can be accurately reconstructed using end-to-end transformer based methods on a simulated calorimeter dataset. We evaluate and compare three distinct machine learning frameworks, focusing on two generative architectures: diffusion and flow matching as well as query-based set prediction. Our results demonstrate that these advanced methods provide highly effective and scalable alternatives for resolving complex overlapping particle showers in conditions encountered in future calorimeters.
item.dc:creator: Qiming Bao, Haotian Bi, Benedikt Maier, Alex Tapper, Lauri Laatu

item.title: Quantum Correlations Between Two Giant Dipole Resonances in Ultra-Peripheral Collisions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mutual Coulomb dissociation in ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions is dominated by Giant Dipole Resonance (GDR) excitation, whose subsequent decays produce forward neutrons. Standard descriptions treat the two GDRs excited in opposite nuclei as statistically independent, leading primarily to a quadrupolar azimuthal correlation determined by the common photon-polarization axis. In this work, we investigate the possibility that the two GDRs are instead prepared with a correlated quantum phase during the overlap of the electromagnetic pulses. We develop a phase-sensitive GDR decay model and implement it in a modified version of the \texttt{$n_{0}^{0}n$} Monte Carlo generator, allowing a quantitative comparison among three competing mechanisms: the weak dipolar modulation from electromagnetic recoil, the quadrupolar correlation from independent polarized GDR decays, and the phase-sensitive dipolar modulation associated with the proposed phase-lock scenario. For neutron pairs with small relative emission-time differences, the correlated-phase scenario produces a pronounced first-harmonic modulation in the two-neutron relative-azimuth distribution. Averaging over all relative emission times substantially reduces this modulation. Within the adopted energy-dependent angular model, the time-selected dipolar coefficient increases in magnitude with pair-mean neutron kinetic energy. These results identify neutron relative-azimuth correlations and their energy dependence as experimentally accessible observables for probing quantum phase correlations between the two GDR excitations. Such phase-sensitive correlations could also provide a basis for future tests of quantum entanglement between spatially separated GDR excitations at RHIC and the LHC.

item.title: Search for $^4\overline{\mathrm{Li}}$ from $\overline{\mathrm{p}}+{}^3\overline{\mathrm{He}}$ femtoscopy in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}} =5.36$ TeV with ALICE
item.description: arXiv:2610.38549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In these proceedings, the search for $^4\overline{\mathrm{Li}}$ in Pb-Pb collisions with ALICE is presented. The particle is reconstructed via its two-body decay channel $^4\overline{\mathrm{Li}} \rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{p}} + {}^3\overline{\mathrm{He}}$, using femtoscopic correlations. A dedicated analysis procedure has been developed to subtract the correlated and uncorrelated $\overline{\mathrm{p}} + ^3\overline{\mathrm{He}}$ combinatorial background. The production yield of $^4\overline{\mathrm{Li}}$ is compared with that of $^4\overline{\mathrm{He}}$. Owing to the presence of several $^4\mathrm{Li}$ resonances and their spin degeneracy, the production of $^4\overline{\mathrm{Li}}$ is expected to be enhanced with respect to the compact $^4\overline{\mathrm{He}}$, making this new measurement a sensitive probe for testing nucleosynthesis models in high-energy hadronic collisions.

item.title: Exploring and optimizing the Vivado Flow on large FPGA designs: A Practical Analysis of Strategies and Their Impact on Timing
item.description: arXiv:2610.38575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Achieving timing closure in FPGA designs is crucial, especially for high-performance applications. The Vivado Design Suite offers several strategies for optimization, but finding the best configuration for a given project remains challenging. This paper explores the various Vivado's timing directives and strategies to improve performance across timing, area, and runtime. Through two test-case designs, an NQR spectrometer SoC-FPGA and a digital readout ASIC prototype for high energy physics particle detector's, different strategies and configurations are compared to identify the most efficient flow.

item.title: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays
item.description: arXiv:2610.38660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a new method to search for fifth forces at micron scales, by resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms in optical tweezer arrays. We develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry, which can approach the Standard Quantum Limit, and expand the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints. We show that this level of sensitivity can also probe well-motivated models of extra dimensions beyond the current tabletop state of the art, by leveraging the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.
item.dc:creator: Marios Galanis, Andrew A. Geraci

item.title: Collinear Factorization and Evolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.38666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The method of collinear factorization for high-energy inclusive cross sections has found wide use in the analysis of hadronic collisions. We introduce the form of factorized cross sections, and discuss the roles and definitions of parton distributions, hadronic fragmentation functions, and their evolution, starting with parton model concepts. The Drell-Yan process is used to illustrate the calculation of QCD corrections at next-to-leading order. The special role of deep-inelastic scattering structure functions and their relation to hadronic structure are also briefly discussed. We provide an introduction to all-order arguments for factorization and infrared safety, and close with a brief review of related factorization formalisms.
item.dc:creator: George Sterman, Zhite Yu

item.title: Precision Studies of Boosted Polarized Vector Bosons with Energy Correlators
item.description: arXiv:2610.38688v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Boosted, hadronically decaying $W$ and $Z$ bosons are among the most abundant heavy objects at colliders, and their vector nature makes their substructure qualitatively richer than that of a scalar. We initiate precision studies of the hadronic decays of boosted polarized vector bosons with energy correlators. In the narrow-width limit, the laboratory-frame two-point energy correlator is a sum of longitudinal and transverse decay spectra, each weighted by its polarized production rate and obtained by a closed-form boost kernel acting on rest-frame correlators. Combining polarized production density matrices, computed at NNLO in QCD for $pp\to V+X$ and at leading order for $e^+e^-\to W^+W^-$, with decay correlators that combine NNLO fixed order with NNLL collinear and N$^4$LL back-to-back resummation, we find for high-$p_T$ $W/Z$ production that polarization shifts the spectrum by $\mathcal{O}(10\%)$ relative to a naive unpolarized treatment. Even without any reconstruction, hadronic $W/Z$ decays stand out over the realistic QCD background of untagged jet samples as a localized angular bump. Our results open the door to using energy correlators for polarimetry of electroweak bosons through their hadronic decays, for standard-candle measurements of electroweak bosons inside jets, and in sharper searches for new resonances.
item.dc:creator: Anjie Gao, Kyle Lee, Xiaoyuan Zhang

item.title: Positive-weight moment matching at NNLO and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.38712v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parton-shower simulations at state-of-the-art perturbative accuracy carry many negative event weights, which dilute their statistical power. For many purposes, this makes them unusable. We formulate a method for the generation of positive-weighted event samples which reproduce, up to a controllable approximation, suites of IR-safe observables with the highest perturbative accuracy of any available calculation. This method is arbitrarily differential in phase space, and free from unphysical artefacts such as binning-dependence. Applied to a leading-order Pythia sample, the method gives simultaneous NNLO accuracy for Drell--Yan and $Z+\text{jet}$ observables in a positive-weighted event sample, for the first time. The method generalises immediately to higher orders of perturbation theory, higher multiplicities, and other processes, observables, and event generators.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Assi, Rene Poncelet, James Whitehead

item.title: Searching for Dark Photons and ALPs using Gamma-rays from Nuclear Reactors
item.description: arXiv:2610.38745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nuclear reactors are intense sources of MeV gamma rays, produced in fission, radiative neutron capture and the de-excitation of fission products. Building on earlier phenomenological studies, we present a detector-independent description of the production of light, weakly coupled particles by reactor gamma rays and of their detection through scattering, absorption and decay in a nearby detector. We consider kinetically mixed dark photons, produced and detected through Compton-like processes, and axion-like particles (ALPs) coupled to photons, electrons and nucleons, produced through Primakoff conversion, Compton-like scattering and magnetic nuclear transitions such as the $2.23~\mathrm{MeV}$ line of $p(n,\gamma)d$. As a concrete application, we derive the projected sensitivities of the CONUS+ germanium experiment at the Leibstadt reactor and of a conceivable $100$-kg CONUS100 upgrade. For sub-MeV dark photons, CONUS+ and CONUS100 reach kinetic mixings of $\epsilon\simeq1.65\times10^{-5}$ and $1.2\times10^{-5}$, respectively, for $0.5~\mathrm{keV}\lesssim m_{A'}\lesssim0.5~\mathrm{MeV}$. For ALPs, we show that CONUS100 can probe an unexplored region of parameter space at MeV masses, in particular through $a\to e^+e^-$ decays of ALPs emitted in the deuteron line, assuming a energy window extended to $10~\mathrm{MeV}$.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Angel, Manfred Lindner, Farinaldo S. Queiroz, Bilge S. Solak

item.title: Predicting $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ states from a reanalysis of lattice QCD data
item.description: arXiv:2610.38750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We reanalyze the lattice QCD data for the isoscalar $\bar b\bar c ud$ systems with $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ at $m_{\pi}\simeq 220$ MeV, incorporating both short- and long-range interactions constrained by heavy-quark spin and chiral symmetries. Using the interaction fitted to the lattice results, we predict a spectrum of isoscalar $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ molecular states with quantum numbers $J^P=0^+$, $1^+$, and $2^+$. The predicted $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $B\bar D$ and $B^*\bar D$ bound states are consistent with the lattice results. Furthermore, the two resonances reported by the lattice collaboration in the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $\bar b\bar c ud$ channels can be naturally interpreted as $B^*\bar D{}^*$ and $B\bar D{}^*$ hadronic molecules, respectively. We also predict two previously unreported $B^*\bar D{}^*$ states with $J^P=1^+$ and $2^+$: a bound state and a shallow state whose pole may correspond to either a virtual state or a bound state, respectively. Our results provide a unified interpretation of the lattice spectrum and highlight the interplay between short- and long-range interactions in the dynamics of the $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ systems.

item.title: Linking a 152 GeV diphoton excess to dark matter and gravitational waves in the singlet-extended 2HDM
item.description: arXiv:2610.39057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the diphoton excesses near $152~\mathrm{GeV}$ accompanied by missing transverse momentum (MET) in the Type-I two-Higgs-doublet model extended by a complex scalar singlet, whose imaginary component serves as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone dark matter (DM) candidate $\chi$. The signal arises from the cascade process $gg\to h_3\to h_2h_2\to\gamma\gamma\chi\chi$, where $h_2$ is the scalar resonance near $152~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $h_3$ is a heavier CP-even scalar. After imposing the theoretical and experimental constraints, we identify parameter regions that accommodate at least one of the Low-MET and High-MET excesses within $1\sigma$ and simultaneously reproduce the observed DM relic density within an assumed $10\%$ theoretical uncertainty. A subset of these samples supports first-order electroweak phase transitions with substantial supercooling. For a three-year observation, selected samples yield gravitational-wave signals with signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) above $10$ at LISA, TianQin, DECIGO, and BBO. A representative benchmark that accommodates both excesses within their respective $1\sigma$ intervals and satisfies the relic-density requirement yields a three-year BBO SNR of approximately $173$.
item.dc:creator: Yabo Dong, Jun Fan, Kun Wang, Haijun Yang, Jingya Zhu

item.title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
item.description: arXiv:2610.39094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

item.title: A doubly charmed strange molecule from coupled-channel dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.39143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a doubly charmed molecular state $T_{cc\bar{s}}$ with $C=+2$, $\mathcal{S}=+1$, and $I=1/2$ in an off-shell coupled-channel formalism. Constructing the interaction kernel from a meson-exchange model based on an effective Lagrangian and solving the coupled-channel scattering equation in the Blankenbecler-Sugar reduction, we find a pole only for $J^P=1^+$ among $J^P=0^\pm$, $1^\pm$, and $2^\pm$. With the reduced cutoff mass of $600$~MeV, we obtain a mass of $3972.90$~MeV, which corresponds to a binding energy of $4.01$~MeV relative to the $D^*D_s$ threshold. Examining the relative signs and magnitudes of the $S$-wave channel couplings extracted from the pole residues, we demonstrate that the pole belongs predominantly to the triplet ($\mathbf{3}_A$) representation. We also discuss the relevance of heavy-quark spin symmetry to the bound state.
item.dc:creator: Hee-Jin Kim, Hyun-Chul Kim

item.title: Position- and Temperature-Dependent Responsivity in a KID-Based Phonon-Mediated Detector
item.description: arXiv:2610.39338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report on the position- and temperature-dependent response of a kinetic inductance phonon-mediated (KIPM) detector. To study position-dependence, we used a controllable mirror attached to a micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) to steer optical light with a 100 $\mu$m spot size over the backside of the cryogenic detector. With both pulsed and continuous operation of the LED, we observe features of the detector housing and find that the signal is strongest when the LED is pointed directly at the KID. The "off-KID" response is measured to be 34% of the "on-KID" response and is largely independent of direction. We model phonon propagation and collection in the KIPM detector with G4CMP and assert that the isotropic angular dependence is unlikely to be due to discrete phonon absorption "sinks", such as the microwave feedline or the device mounting points, but can be explained instead by an isotropic energy loss in the crystal. We furthermore utilize the temperature flexibility of the MEMS and KIPM detector system to investigate temperature-dependent responsivity, both at the sensor level (i.e., frequency shifts in the KID) and at the detector level (i.e., position dependence). We fit the KID's response to a two-component heat capacity and present the model as an alternative way to understand the KID's response to absorbed energy. We show on- and off-KID data at a range of temperatures and show that the phonon dynamics are not temperature dependent. We comment on the resulting implication for KID dynamics and design improvements.

item.title: Manifestation of near-threshold $\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$ resonances in $e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}\eta$ process
item.description: arXiv:2610.39526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is shown that the invariant-mass distribution of $\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$ pairs in the process $e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}\eta$ can be explained by near-threshold resonances with quantum numbers $J^{PC}=1^{--}$ and $J^{PC}=1^{+-}$. The resonance with $J^{PC}=1^{--}$ corresponds to a loosely bound state, while the resonance with $J^{PC}=1^{+-}$ is a virtual state above the threshold. Accounting for both resonances results in good agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental data. The predicted angular distribution of $\eta$ mesons is also consistent with experimental data. It is shown that in our model there is a strong dependence of $\eta$-meson angular distribution on the invariant mass of $\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$ pair.

item.title: A flexible electronics and DAQ system for the Timepix4 ASIC
item.description: arXiv:2610.39706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The INFN Data Acquisition system (IDAQ) is designed for data-driven readout of the Timepix4 ASIC, supporting simultaneous time-of-arrival and time-over-threshold measurements with nanosecond precision. The system architecture combines dedicated hardware for high-speed serial data transmission, FPGA-based data processing, and a Trigger Logic Unit for synchronization and timing distribution. It operates in continuous streaming and triggered modes, ensuring low-latency and high-throughput performance. The system has been deployed in test-beam campaigns within the 4DPHOTON project, demonstrating stable operation, precise timing alignment, and reliable data handling under high-rate conditions.

item.title: Search for Cosmic Rays in GRANDProto300
item.description: arXiv:2610.39720v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GRANDProto300 is a prototype array of the GRAND experiment, designed to validate the technique of autonomous radio-detection of astroparticles by detecting cosmic rays with energies between 10$^{17} - 10^{18.5}$ eV. This observation will further enable the study of the Galactic-to-extragalactic source transition region. Between November 2024 and June 2025, 46 antennas were operational, and since July 2025, 63 antennas have been collecting data stably. We present here our cosmic-ray search pipeline, that involves several filtering steps: (1) exclusion of clustered (in time and space) noise events, (2) polarization cut, (3) zenith arrival cut, and (4) delay in expected trigger cut. The efficiency is evaluated on the latest batch of data from July 2025 to October 2025. Additionally, we present an identification layer that is being developed: a CNN-based algorithm to discriminate between noise and cosmic-ray signals, using signal traces. We present the accuracy of our model, trained both on simulations and on real cosmic-ray signal datasets.

item.title: $P$--wave quarkonia in jets at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2610.39959v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first systematic theoretical study of the production of $P$-wave charmonium states $\chi_{cJ}$ and bottomonium states $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ within jets at the LHC using the fragmenting jet function framework at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$. Our calculation resums both collinear DGLAP logarithms and threshold double logarithms in the fragmentation functions and accounts for feeddown contributions from higher quarkonium states. We observe a notable contrast between the charmonium and bottomonium sectors. For $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$, the normalized momentum-fraction distributions exhibit a nearly universal shape, with remarkably weak dependence on the choice of long-distance matrix element sets, the radial excitation ($n=1,2,3$), and the total angular momentum ($J=0,1,2$). We attribute this universality to the overwhelming dominance of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ fragmentation channel, while feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states remain small. In contrast, the shape of $\chi_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $\chi_{cJ}$ and $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. We also compare our predictions with \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations for selected $P$-wave quarkonium states.
item.dc:creator: Taewook Ha, Byungsik Hong, Daekyoung Kang, Soohwan Lee, Bayu Adi Nugraha Putra

item.title: Denoising Graph Super-Resolution towards Improved Collider Event Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2409.16052v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In preparation for Higgs factories and energy-frontier facilities, future colliders are moving toward high-granularity calorimeters to improve reconstruction quality. However, the cost and construction complexity of such detectors is substantial, making software-based approaches like superresolution an attractive complementary tool. This study explores integrating superresolution techniques into an LHC-like reconstruction pipeline to effectively enhance calorimeter granularity and suppress noise. We find that this software preprocessing step significantly improves reconstruction quality at fixed detector granularity, narrowing the performance gap to a finer calorimeter without closing it. To demonstrate its impact, we propose a novel transformer-based particle-flow model that offers improved particle reconstruction quality and interpretability. Our results serve as a proof of concept, demonstrating the potential of superresolution to enhance reconstruction in collider environments.
item.dc:creator: Nilotpal Kakati, Etienne Dreyer, Eilam Gross

item.title: Observation of a cross-section enhancement near the $t\bar{t}$ production threshold in $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
item.description: arXiv:2601.11780v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A measurement of $t\bar{t}$ production is presented in the invariant-mass region near the pair production threshold, $m_{t\bar{t}} \sim 345$ GeV, in final states with two charged leptons and multiple jets. The measurement is based on $140\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data collected at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The data are compared to two models of $t\bar{t}$ production: a baseline model including only perturbative QCD predictions for the hard process at approximate next-to-next-to leading order accuracy in the strong coupling, and an extended model that, in addition, incorporates non-relativistic QCD simulations that also include the formation of colour-singlet quasi-bound-states near the $t\bar{t}$ threshold. The agreement between the data and the models is quantified via a profile-likelihood fit to the reconstructed $m_{t\bar{t}}$ distributions, in bins of two angular observables sensitive to spin-correlations in the $t\bar{t}$ system. An excess of events is observed over the baseline perturbative QCD prediction, with an observed significance over $8$ standard deviations. This excess is consistent with the formation of colour-singlet and spin-singlet $S$-wave quasi-bound $t\bar{t}$ states, as predicted by non-relativistic QCD, and corresponds to an observed cross-section of $9.3^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ pb.

item.title: Measurement of Born Cross Sections for $e^+e^- \to K^+\Xi^0\bar\Sigma^-$ at $\sqrt{s} = 3.51-4.95$ GeV and Observation of $\psi(3770) \to K^+\Xi^0\bar\Sigma^-$
item.description: arXiv:2605.19780v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using 44.55 fb$^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first measurement of the Born cross sections for the $e^+e^- \to K^+\Xi^0\bar\Sigma^-$ reaction at fifty-six center-of-mass energies between 3.51 and 4.95~GeV. A fit to the dressed cross sections reveals the first observation of the $\psi(3770) \to K^+\Xi^0\bar\Sigma^-$ process, with a statistical significance of 6.0$\sigma$ including systematic uncertainties. This result represents the first observation of charmless three-body baryonic decay of a vector charmonium state above the open-charm threshold. No significant signals for other charmonium(-like) states i.e., $\psi(4040)$, $\psi(4160)$, $Y(4230)$, $Y(4360)$, $\psi(4415)$, $Y(4500)$, $Y(4660)$ or $Y(4710)$ are observed, and the upper limits for the product of the branching fraction and the electronic partial width at the 90% confidence level for each assumed charmonium(-like) state are provided. Additionally, the ratios of Born cross sections between this work and the previous measurements of $e^+e^- \to K^{0}_{S}\bar\Xi^{-}\Sigma^-$ and $K^-\bar\Xi^+\bar\Sigma^0$ are provided, which can be used to validate theoretical predictions related to isospin symmetry.

item.title: First measurement of the masses of the $\Upsilon_1(1D)$ and $\Upsilon_3(1D)$ states and the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\eta$ and $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\pi^+\pi^-$
item.description: arXiv:2607.04369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the processes $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\eta$ and $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\pi^+\pi^-$ at center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s}$=(10.73 -- 11.02) GeV using a $142.5\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ data sample, including 122~fb$^{-1}$ near the $\Upsilon$(10860) peak ($\sqrt{s}$ = 10.866 GeV), collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy $e^+e^-$ collider. From the peak sample, the products of Born cross section times branching fraction are obtained for $\sigma_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\eta)$ or $\sigma_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\pi^+\pi^-)$ and ${\cal B}(\Upsilon_J(1D)\to\chi_{b1}\gamma)$ or ${\cal B}(\Upsilon_J(1D)\to\chi_{b2}\gamma)$ for each $\Upsilon_J(1D)$ state. The corresponding branching fractions for $\Upsilon(10860)$ decays are also obtained. The significances of the $\Upsilon_1(1D)$, $\Upsilon_2(1D)$, and $\Upsilon_3(1D)$ signals are 4.8$\sigma$, ${>}10\sigma$, and 3.0$\sigma$, respectively, including systematic uncertainties. The mass for $\Upsilon_2(1D)$ is measured to be $(10167.0\pm 1.0\pm 0.2)$ MeV/$c^2$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic. The mass splittings $\Delta m_{12}=m(\Upsilon_2(1D))-m(\Upsilon_1(1D))$ and $\Delta m_{23}=m(\Upsilon_3(1D))-m(\Upsilon_2(1D))$ are $(11.8\pm1.5\pm0.4)$ MeV/$c^2$ and $(7.6\pm2.4\pm0.6)$ MeV/$c^2$, respectively.~We determine the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\eta$ and $e^+e^-\to\Upsilon_J(1D)\pi^+\pi^-$ for the $\Upsilon_1(1D)$, $\Upsilon_2(1D)$, and $\Upsilon_3(1D)$ states, combined.

item.title: Axion-Like Particle Search with a Hybrid Cherenkov-Scintillation Detector
item.description: arXiv:2608.12616v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This analysis presents the first proof-of-concept search for axion-like particles (ALPs) using a hybrid Cherenkov-scintillation detector at a beam-dump facility. The work is based on the Coherent CAPTAIN-Mills (CCM) experiment, a 10-ton liquid argon light collection detector located at Los Alamos National Laboratory. The CCM200 detector is instrumented with 200 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs), providing approximately 50% photocathode coverage. To enable optical discrimination, 80% of the PMTs are coated with a wavelength-shifting material while the remaining 20% are left uncoated. This configuration, combined with nanosecond-scale timing resolution, provides sensitivity to prompt Cherenkov radiation while maintaining efficient detection of liquid argon scintillation light [1, 2]. This analysis constructs four observables that exploit the Cherenkov emission and event topology expected from ALP-induced electromagnetic interactions. These observables are combined into a likelihood-ratio classifier that provides powerful rejection of steady-state backgrounds. No statistically significant excess above the expected background prediction is observed for $10^{-3}~\mathrm{MeV} < m_a < 10~\mathrm{MeV}$. Nevertheless, the improved background rejection enabled by hybrid Cherenkov-scintillation detection allows this analysis to surpass the sensitivity of the previous CCM120 search [3] despite less exposure and demonstrate the physics potential for hybrid Cherenkov-scintillation detectors.

item.title: Neutralino dark matter in gauge mediation
item.description: arXiv:2502.07539v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explore the potential of neutralino dark matter within the framework of gauge-mediated supersymmetry (SUSY) breaking. Gauge mediation offers an advantage over gravity mediation, as SUSY CP/flavor problems are avoided more easily, leading to significantly milder fine-tuning for electroweak symmetry-breaking compared to gravity mediation. In our models, the lightest neutralino, as the lightest SUSY particle (LSP), is a viable dark matter candidate, assuming a gravitino mass of $\mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{TeV}$. The models are formulated in five-dimensional space-time, where the SUSY breaking field and the matter fields are placed on separate branes to avoid issues related to flavor and CP violation, and the radion is stabilized by a supersymmetric Goldberger--Wise mechanism. Four distinct neutralino dark matter scenarios are studied: bino-wino coannihilation, higgsino dark matter, wino dark matter, and entropy-diluted bino dark matter. For each case, we determine the allowed parameter spaces and evaluate their consistency with existing experimental limits. Additionally, we examine the potential for testing these models through future investigations at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) and through dark matter direct detection experiments.

item.title: Dark Parton Shower Effects for Cosmic Ray Boosted Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2509.12007v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the effects of dark parton showers on the direct detection of cosmic-ray boosted dark matter (CRDM), focusing on a dark-photon-mediated model with fermionic dark matter--electron interactions. Using a Monte Carlo framework to incorporate Sudakov form factors and kinematic dipole recoil schemes, we simulate the evolution of the CRDM energy spectrum under dark sector splitting. Our results reveal that dark parton showering induces an energy-dependent reshaping of the CRDM flux, particularly characterized by a depletion of the high-energy flux. For a dark matter (DM) mass of 1 keV and a coupling of $g_D=3$, the CRDM flux can be enhanced by up to a factor of 1.12 in the $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2} \sim 1)$ MeV energy range for $2m_\chi \lesssim m_{A^\prime} \lesssim 10^{-2}$ MeV, whereas it is suppressed by more than 50% at energies around 100 MeV for $m_{A^\prime} \lesssim 10^{-3}$ MeV. We then translate these effects into experimental sensitivities for PandaX-4T, Super-Kamiokande, and JUNO. For $m_{A^\prime} = 10^{-3}$ MeV and $g_D=3$, the bounds on the kinetic mixing parameter $\epsilon^2$ are relaxed by factors of 1.02, 1.6, and 1.4, respectively. Incorporating the effects of DM parton distribution functions (PDFs) at neutrino detectors alongside dark parton shower effects further relaxes these bounds.

item.title: Melting LHC detectors: A novel search for stopped long-lived particles
item.description: arXiv:2512.12023v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Particles at the TeV scale with lifetimes of a year or longer could have been abundantly produced at the LHC yet escaped detection because of backgrounds, and could still be trapped within detector materials. With gluinos in split supersymmetry as a working example, we show that these trapped particles can be recovered from detector materials once prepared in liquid form, for example, by melting silicon detectors, extracting liquid argon from the electromagnetic calorimeter, or constructing a large water pool near ATLAS or CMS. These liquid samples can then be processed using iterative centrifugation followed by mass spectrometry, enabling single-particle sensitivity in macroscopic samples. This method can potentially discover gluinos up to 3 TeV in mass at the HL-LHC. It can also improve upon existing limits for other long-lived particles. For example, it can discover the stop up to 2 TeV, and will also be sensitive to integer-charged particles in the TeV range.

item.title: Performance Benchmarks for 2-View and 3-View Fiber-Projection Fine-Grained Particle Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2601.07633v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fine-grained scintillator detectors are critical for precision measurements in nuclear and particle physics, where accurate reconstruction of interaction vertices and secondary particle directions enables separation of signal from background events. A well-known design choice is the fiber readout geometry: traditional 2-View systems use orthogonal X and Y fibers, while next-generation 3-View designs add a third Z-fiber layer that provides unambiguous 3D voxel identification. The 2-View approach suffers from combinatorial ''ghost hits'', which are false 3D candidates arising from fiber projection ambiguities, that degrade reconstruction performance in high-multiplicity events. This paper presents comprehensive simulation benchmarks quantifying the performance difference between 2-View and 3-View geometries across key metrics. We find that the 3-View geometry reduces ghost hits by 30 to 90% depending on event topology, provides robust vertex resolution across complex topologies, and maintains superior angular resolution for shower direction reconstruction. These benchmarks inform the design optimization of future detectors and provide quantitative guidance for reconstruction algorithm development across a broad range of experiments including neutrino physics, rare kaon/pion decays, and collider calorimetry.

item.title: Precision Isotope-Shift Measurement of the ${}^1S_0 \leftrightarrow {}^3P_2$ Transition and a Multi-Transition King-Plot Consistency Test
item.description: arXiv:2601.08487v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present precision spectroscopy and isotope shift measurement of the ${}^1S_0 \leftrightarrow {}^3P_2$ clock transition in neutral ytterbium ($\mathrm{Yb}$) atoms. By revealing a magic wavelength at $905.4(2)$ nm, we successfully achieve the atomic spectrum narrower than $100$ Hz. The interleaved clock operation between isotopes allows us to determine isotope shifts of four bosonic isotope pairs at Hz-level uncertainties, which is combined with those of other four ultra-narrow transitions in $\mathrm{Yb}$ and $\mathrm{Yb}^+$ to construct the King plot. We show that a rich dataset spanning multiple transitions enables a test of a restricted isotope-shift ansatz comprising the leading mass and field shifts, one effective factorized higher-order Standard Model contribution, and a new-particle contribution. Within this ansatz, the five-transition data are inconsistent with the new-particle contribution serving as the sole additional contribution over the mass ranges $m_\phi \leq 6.5$ keV and $18$ keV $\leq m_\phi < 100$ keV, while the previous works rely on another bound set by the neutron scattering and $(g-2)_e$ measurements. This work paves the way for the effective use of precision isotope shift data in the King plot analysis and stimulates further measurements in Yb and other elements.

item.title: Long-term scintillation light performance, calibrations, and triggering efficiency in the MicroBooNE detector
item.description: arXiv:2603.23691v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A detailed understanding of scintillation light in liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs) is essential for the robust extraction of physics measurements from their data. This article presents the long-term performance of scintillation light production and detection using five years of data from the MicroBooNE LArTPC neutrino detector. We describe the MicroBooNE light simulation and light-based triggering schemes, and present the photomultiplier tube gain calibration and stability, light response stability, and light-based systematic uncertainties over the course of five years of data collection. We also make an in-situ measurement of the scintillation light triggering efficiency down to 30 MeV of visible energy. Finally, we discuss two notable observations in MicroBooNE's data, both reported here for the first time: an approximately 50\% decline in MicroBooNE's light yield over time, concentrated in the first two years of running; and a higher than expected O(200 kHz) rate of single photoelectrons (SPE). We present the first measurements of the dependence of the SPE rate on the TPC electric field strength and polarity. Together, the results presented in this article provide an important benchmark for the long-term performance of scintillation light systems in LArTPCs and their use in particle physics measurements.

item.title: Deeply virtual meson production at HERA and at the EIC within the Color Glass Condensate EFT
item.description: arXiv:2603.25363v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continuing our previous study of Deeply Virtual Meson Production (DVMP) at twist-3 accuracy, we derive compact expressions for all helicity amplitudes. We perform a phenomenological analysis of the helicity-amplitude ratio $\mathcal{A}^{11}/\mathcal{A}^{00}$ and of the spin-density matrix element $r_{00}^{04}$ within the Color Glass Condensate framework. Small-$x$ evolution is incorporated by numerically solving the running-coupling-and-collinearly-improved Balitsky-Kovchegov and Balitsky-Fadin-Kuraev-Lipatov equations with the McLerran-Venugopalan model as the initial condition. Our exploratory phenomenological study shows that parameters fitted to inclusive DIS data capture the shape of the measured helicity observables but overestimate their magnitude, indicating the need for a dedicated fit to exclusive data. To overcome its absence in the literature, we introduce an effective phenomenological matching prescription. Our results are then compared to HERA data, and predictions are presented for electron-lead collisions at the future Electron-Ion Collider. We discuss the impact of non-linear effects at low photon virtuality and the role of genuine higher-twist contributions associated with light vector meson distribution amplitudes, corresponding to higher-Fock-state components of the projectile.

item.title: Lepton Flavor Violating Higgs decays at the Compact Linear Collider
item.description: arXiv:2605.08501v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lepton flavor violating Higgs decays could appear in scenarios beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. In this article, we study the sensitivity of a future Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) to such processes, namely, $h\rightarrow e\mu$, $h\rightarrow\tau\mu$, and $h\rightarrow e\tau$. In the absence of any observation, 95\% CL\ upper limits in the region of $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-5}$ could be placed on the branching fractions of these processes, assuming integrated luminosities of $4$\,ab$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=1.4$ TeV and $5$\,ab$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=3$ TeV.

item.title: Comprehensive study of timing resolution in plastic scintillator detectors with wavelength-shifting fiber and silicon photomultiplier readout
item.description: arXiv:2607.14290v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a comprehensive study of the timing resolution achievable in plastic scintillator detectors read out through wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibers coupled to silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), combining a semi-analytical framework, toy Monte Carlo validation, and full Geant4 optical photon simulation. The analytical model traces the complete photon detection chain: scintillation emission, WLS fiber re-emission, optical transit time dispersion, SiPM single-photon time resolution, and electronics quantization. It expresses the timing resolution $\sigt$ as a function of the detected photoelectron yield $\Npe$, scintillator decay constants ($\taur$, $\taud$), WLS re-emission time ($\tauwls$), fiber numerical aperture, detector geometry, and readout electronics parameters. The analytical predictions are validated at two levels. First, toy Monte Carlo simulations ($2\times 10^5$ events per parameter point across 80 grid points spanning 8 fiber types and $\Npe$ from 5 to 200) achieve analytical-to-MC agreement of \add{$1.0000 \pm 0.0018$}. Second, full Geant4 optical photon simulations track the entire scintillation, wavelength-shifting, and fiber transport chain in realistic detector geometries, confirming the analytical timing predictions\add{ to within 10--20\% for $\Npe \gtrsim 10$} and providing first-principles photoelectron yield calibration. A comprehensive parameter scan covering 7 scintillator materials, 8 WLS fiber types, 5 SiPM models, 5 electronics configurations, 3 readout topologies, and 3 boundary conditions produces quantitative design maps and lookup tables for detector optimization.

item.title: Electromagnetic form factors of singly charmed baryons $\Sigma_c$ and $\Lambda_c$ in a covariant quark-diquark model
item.description: arXiv:2607.23943v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic study of the spacelike electromagnetic form factors of the ground-state singly charmed baryons, $\Sigma_c$ ($\Sigma_c^{++},\Sigma_c^+,\Sigma_c^0$) and $\Lambda_c^+$, within a covariant quark-diquark model. Based on this framework, we obtain their magnetic moments as well as electric charge and magnetic moment radii. Such observables are important to understand the internal structure and the inner dynamics of these heavy baryon states. Our theoretical calculations are in qualitative agreement with available lattice QCD results of $\Sigma_c^{++}$ and $\Sigma_c^0$ baryons. We also discuss the mechanism behind the dependence of the numerical results on the charm quark and light diquark. A key finding is that the electric form factors of the singly charmed baryons fall off much more slowly with momentum transfer $Q^2$ than that of the proton, indicating a more compact electric charge distribution, which is attributed to the heavy charm quark acting as a localized core. More importantly, we observe a striking difference in the magnetic structure: while the magnetic form factors of $\Sigma_c$ are dominated by the light axial-vector diquark, those of $\Lambda_c^+$ are unexpectedly governed by the charm quark due to the vanishing contribution of the scalar diquark. This highlights the decisive role of the light-diquark spin configuration in determining the magnetic properties. Finally, using an empirical asymptotic relation connecting the spacelike and timelike regions, we predict the total cross section for $e^+e^-\to\Sigma_c\bar{\Sigma}_c$. Our findings can be tested at existing facilities including the BESIII, Belle II and LHCb, as well as the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility.

item.title: The QCD Axion and Neutrino Masses
item.description: arXiv:2608.05150v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The strong CP problem and the origin of neutrino masses are among the clearest motivations for physics beyond the Standard Model. The Peccei-Quinn mechanism offers an elegant dynamical solution to the strong CP problem, predicting the QCD axion, while neutrino masses point to new degrees of freedom or interactions beyond the Standard Model. We explore the possibility that these two phenomena arise from a common origin by identifying the Peccei-Quinn symmetry-breaking scale with the scale responsible for neutrino mass generation. We perform a systematic and unified analysis of this connection in both DFSZ and KSVZ realizations of the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, considering the Type-I, Type-II, and Type-III seesaw mechanisms, the Zee radiative model, and the colored seesaw. For each scenario, we determine the axion couplings to photons and neutrinos and examine their phenomenological consequences. A robust prediction of all the frameworks considered is the existence of axion-neutrino couplings. We show that these interactions can significantly affect the axion decays. If the QCD axion makes up the observed dark matter, these couplings also lead to a large monochromatic neutrino flux from axion decays, opening a complementary path to test these theories in future neutrino experiments.

item.title: Transferable Fast Calorimeter Shower Generation via Multi-Geometry Pre-training
item.description: arXiv:2608.18233v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Detailed Geant4 simulation of calorimeter showers dominates the computing budget of high-energy physics experiments. Deep generative surrogates reduce this cost, but they have remained tied to the detector they were trained on, so each new geometry needs a large in-domain dataset. We study whether a single point cloud shower generator can be pre-trained on multiple detectors and transferred to unseen calorimeters. The pre-training geometries come from synthetic geometric variation rather than real-detector data. We introduce SimpleBox, a family of $10^4$ box calorimeters spanning the plane of sampling fraction and longitudinal segmentation, and benchmark it against pre-training on realistic detectors. On a calorimeter unseen in pre-training, with $10^3$ target showers for fine-tuning, the two priors reduce the aggregated sliced Wasserstein distance to Geant4 by factors of 5.2 (synthetic) and 8.0 (realistic) relative to training from scratch. At larger target sizes the synthetic prior performs better than the realistic one. Geometric diversity alone is therefore a practical way to pre-train a transferable shower generator.

item.title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow \phi(K^{+}K^{-})\eta' (\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\eta)$ at a future high-luminosity Z factory
item.description: arXiv:2610.27996v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The decay $B_s^0 \to \phi(K^+K^-)\eta'(\pi^+\pi^-\eta)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $\eta$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency. In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $\eta$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined. The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.

item.title: Accelerating fits in high-energy physics and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.35927v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Data analysis in particle physics often involves optimizing a loss function that quantifies how well a theoretical model describes the observed data, in order to estimate the parameters of the model. This is referred to as fitting. As datasets grow larger and more expensive analysis methods are used, the time required to perform this parameter estimation can be a limiting factor. This work explores techniques for accelerating the fitting process, and measures their performance on a set of models representative of a variety of physics fits. We compare the speed and precision of variants of well-known optimization algorithms, namely Newton's method, BFGS, and the Migrad algorithm (commonly used in particle physics fits). We observe significant speedups when using some algorithms: most notably, some variants of BFGS are about ten times faster than Migrad, while achieving the same precision. For quasi-Newtonian algorithms like BFGS and Migrad, we find that the initial value of the Hessian matrix has a large impact on the runtime. We additionally discuss methods for accelerating the evaluation of the loss function and its derivatives, using algebraic simplifications, automatic differentiation, and modern hardware features. We explore techniques for achieving good precision with 32-bit operations, which can achieve significantly higher throughput on the GPU. Lastly we explore efficient parallelization strategies for the CPU and GPU. All of the techniques and algorithms in this paper are implemented in our new FastFit library, which was used for all of our benchmarks.
